title: Normalization and simultaneous models for finite coefficient-system operations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

These whole-system operations preserve normalization, with precisely the following adjoint transition maps:
$$q_W^*T_W(A,N)_m\xrightarrow{\sim}q_W^*A_m\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}q_W^*N_m\xrightarrow{\alpha^A_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^N_{m,n}}T_W(A,N)_n,$$
$$q_X^*Lf_m^*C_m\xrightarrow{\kappa^{-1}}Lf_n^*q_Y^*C_m\xrightarrow{Lf_n^*(\alpha^C_{m,n})}Lf_n^*C_n.$$
The first arrow in the first display is monoidal scalar extension. The coefficient square defining $\kappa$ commutes by the constant-section ring maps; $\kappa$ is the scalar-association map from $Lf_n^*q_Y^*$ to $q_X^*Lf_m^*$, whose inverse inserts $1$ in the intermediate scalar factor [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. The actual input transition factors as $C_m\to\operatorname{Res}q_Y^*C_m\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}\alpha^C_{m,n}}\operatorname{Res}C_n$; the displayed adjoints specify the actual output transitions, not a replacement by canonical scalar-extension units. On flat representatives the tensor adjoint sends $(a\otimes x)\otimes b$ to $\tau_A(a)\otimes b\tau_N(x)$. For $r\ge m\ge n$ both composite output adjoints agree with the direct one: the tensor formula uses the two input cocycles and $q_{r,n}=q_{m,n}q_{r,m}$, and both pullback scalar-association composites multiply the same three scalar factors and then use the input cocycle. The unit adjoint is $B_{W,m}\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}\cong B_{W,n}$.

All these comparisons and cocycles are constructed on whole systems before evaluation. Flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] may be chosen on the ringed sites; every finite iterated tensor or pullback, including coefficient-quotient pullback, is computed on such representatives by ordinary direct-sum total tensor and termwise inverse image. The resulting representatives remain flat-term K-flat, even for complexes unbounded in both directions; the simultaneous system models retain their transitions and coherence. No flatness of a quotient ring map is assumed.

proof.text: Choose complexes of whole strict semilinear systems representing each input in $D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the ringed sequence site to obtain a whole-system K-flat resolution with flat terms; [lem-pur-system-evaluation-kflat] ensures that it is a quasi-isomorphic system complex $P_\bullet$ whose every $P_n$ is K-flat with flat terms. The replacement is a morphism of systems, so its chain transitions $\tau^P_{m,n}$ represent the original transitions and satisfy the identity and quotient composition laws as chain maps. In particular we have not chosen unrelated level resolutions. By [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], whole-system tensor and inverse image exist and evaluate to the stated level operations. We use these whole-system operations on the chosen models throughout.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), applied on the ringed sequence site; whole-system evaluation as in the cited DAG lemmas.

proof.text: For any fixed finite well-typed expression, proceed by structural induction. The input models are supplied by step 1. For a tensor vertex take the ordinary direct-sum total tensor: [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] says that it is again K-flat with flat terms, even with two-sided unbounded inputs, and computes the derived tensor. For a geometric or coefficient-quotient pullback vertex apply the ordinary module pullback termwise. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] hold for both kinds of ringed-topos morphism and give a flat-term K-flat output; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies this computation with the derived pullback. Thus no further level replacements are needed at intermediate vertices. Use the actual induced chain transitions at each vertex. The construction takes place on the ringed sequence topos, and evaluating it gives these same component complexes and transitions.

Let $P_\bullet,Q_\bullet$ represent $A,N$. The actual tensor transition sends $a\otimes x$ to $\tau^P_{m,n}(a)\otimes\tau^Q_{m,n}(x)$. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], its derived adjoint is represented by $(a\otimes x)\otimes b\mapsto\tau^P_{m,n}(a)\otimes b\tau^Q_{m,n}(x)$. Factor this map through the monoidal scalar-extension comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]: first $(a\otimes x)\otimes b\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes(x\otimes b)$, then apply the two input transition adjoints. This is exactly the first displayed transition in the statement. The first map is invertible by the derived monoidal pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity topos with ring map $q_{m,n}$. For normalized inputs, both input adjoints are isomorphisms by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]; their derived tensor is an isomorphism, so the tensor output is normalized.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); scalar unit and adjunct representative normalization in the cited coefficient-adjunction lemma.

proof.text:
For $f:X\to Y$, let $c_j:f^{-1}B_{Y,j}\to B_{X,j}$ be the constant-section structure map. It is invertible by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. The square with $q_Y,q_X$ commutes: both composites send a constant coefficient to its residue at level $n$, and the constant-sheaf universal property gives equality. Apply the coefficient-square comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. For a flat-term K-flat $B_{Y,m}$-complex $P$, its map $\kappa:f_n^*(P\otimes_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n})\to(f_m^*P)\otimes_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n}$ is locally
$$b\otimes(p\otimes a)\longmapsto(1\otimes p)\otimes b c_n(a).$$
Its inverse sends $(s\otimes p)\otimes b$ to $bq_X(s)\otimes(p\otimes1)$. The two composites are identities by balancing; these are degree-zero chain maps. Step 2 permits their use without deriving again, and they are the specified scalar-association comparison and its inverse.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); constant-section coefficient maps as in the cited pro-etale lemma.

proof.text: For the chosen system model $P_\bullet$ of $C$, the actual pullback transition is locally $s\otimes p\mapsto q_X(s)\otimes\tau^P_{m,n}(p)$. Its scalar adjoint is therefore $(s\otimes p)\otimes b\mapsto bq_X(s)\otimes\tau^P_{m,n}(p)$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Using step 4, this is the composite $\kappa^{-1}$ followed by $f_n^*(\alpha^P_{m,n})$, since the latter map sends $bq_X(s)\otimes(p\otimes1)$ to $bq_X(s)\otimes\tau^P_{m,n}(p)$. This proves the second displayed transition formula, including its orientation. The input transition itself factors through $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ followed by its adjunct, as the same adjunction lemma asserts. On localization, $\kappa$ is invertible and $Lf_n^*$ carries the invertible input adjoint to an isomorphism; hence the output is normalized by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. The calculation uses the actual $\tau^P$, not the scalar-insertion unit in its place.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with the scalar-association calculation in step 4 and the normalized representative adjunct formula in the cited node.

proof.text:
For $r\ge m\ge n$, check the tensor cocycle on the chosen system complexes. A local tensor $(a\otimes x)\otimes b\otimes c$, with $b\in B_m,c\in B_n$, goes under the successive adjoints to
$$\tau^P_{r,n}(a)\otimes q_{m,n}(b)c\,\tau^Q_{r,n}(x).$$
The direct adjoint gives the same result after the scalar-association map sends $b\otimes c$ to $q_{m,n}(b)c$. Here we used precisely the two strict input transition cocycles; their derived formulation is that of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. The reassociations are the canonical ones in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. The equality holds on each total-degree summand, commutes with restrictions and sheafification, and hence is an equality of whole-system chain constructions, which remains an equality after localization. At $r=m=n$ the same calculation is the identity.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product) and 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); explicit scalar multiplication and input cocycle calculation.

proof.text:
For pullback the same triple-index check is explicit. On $(s\otimes p)\otimes b\otimes c$, $s\in B_{X,r},b\in B_{X,m},c\in B_{X,n}$, the successive adjoints of step 5 give
$$c q^X_{m,n}(b)q^X_{r,n}(s)\otimes\tau^P_{r,n}(p).$$
The direct adjoint applied after scalar association gives this identical expression, since $q^X_{r,n}=q^X_{m,n}q^X_{r,m}$ and the input transitions satisfy their cocycle [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. This also checks the two possible composites of $\kappa$ maps: step 4 moves scalar factors by multiplication, and both paths multiply these same factors. The canonical comparisons are those of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Balancing and associativity prove equality before localization on the system complexes; the identity index inserts $1$ and gives the identity. No assertion that evaluations detect equality of arbitrary derived morphisms is used.

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); explicit triple-scalar and transition calculation.

proof.text: Finally take the whole-system unit to be $B_\bullet[0]$ with its quotient transitions. Each component has flat terms and is K-flat: tensoring by $B_n[0]$ is the identity functor, so it is exact and preserves acyclic complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its transition adjoint is $B_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n\to B_n$, $s\otimes b\mapsto q_{m,n}(s)b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Multiplication gives both the unit cocycle and identity. The unit comparison agrees with [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. This supplies the unit base case in step 2. Every finite expression thus has simultaneous whole-system models retaining all the transitions just computed. All changes of rings used flat-term K-flat inputs, never flatness of the quotient homomorphism.

Steps 4-5: κ s'⊗(x⊗r)↦(1⊗x)⊗s'φ'(r) has the orientation of lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence.
